sentences.zh: 丽莎，为什么弗吉尼亚州的州长竞选——一场州级竞选，而不是联邦选举——

sentences.en: Why is it being so closely watched and why does it matter to national political reporters like you?
sentences.zh: 会受到如此密切的关注？这对像你这样的全国政治记者来说为什么很重要？

sentences.en: Well, Michael, this is really the first competitive election we've had since
sentences.zh: 嗯，迈克尔，这确实是我们自

sentences.en: Biden won office.
sentences.zh: 拜登上任以来经历的第一次竞争激烈的选举。

sentences.en: And it's also the first race we're seeing without Trump on the ballot or in the
sentences.zh: 这也是我们第一次看到特朗普不在选票上，也不在

sentences.en: White House.
sentences.zh: 白宫里的竞选。

sentences.en: So we're really getting a glimpse of political dynamics that we just haven't tested before of how people are perceiving this moment and how voters are feeling about it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们确实得以一窥此前从未测试过的政治动态，了解人们如何看待这一时刻，以及选民对此有何感受。

sentences.en: And what should we know about the politics of Virginia itself?
sentences.zh: 关于弗吉尼亚州本身的政治，我们应该了解些什么？

sentences.en: So Virginia is an interesting state.
sentences.zh: 弗吉尼亚州是一个有趣的州。

sentences.en: It's traditionally been a red state, but that began to change really during the Obama years.
sentences.zh: 它传统上是一个红州，但这在奥巴马执政期间开始发生真正的变化。

sentences.en: And now, particularly during
sentences.zh: 而现在，特别是在

sentences.en: Trump's time in office, it's become a place that Democrats feel a lot more confident about.
sentences.zh: 特朗普执政期间，它已成为一个让民主党人感到更有信心的州。

sentences.en: It really epitomizes the way that Democrats won during the Trump administration, which was by turning these
sentences.zh: 它确实体现了民主党在特朗普政府期间获胜的方式，那就是通过将这些

sentences.en: suburban counties that had been maybe more moderate or more swing counties, turning them much more democratic.
sentences.zh: 可能更温和或更摇摆的郊区县，转变得更加倾向民主党。

sentences.en: And of course, in 2020, Biden won the state by 10 points.
sentences.zh: 当然，在2020年，拜登以10个百分点的优势赢得了该州。

sentences.en: But there is this sense that
sentences.zh: 但有一种感觉是，

sentences.zh: 弗吉尼亚州是一个深受全国政治环境影响的地方，部分原因是它毗邻华盛顿特区。

sentences.en: And then that gives Republicans a chance to possibly mount a comeback in the Commonwealth, that Republicans could win in Virginia and it could be a harbinger of them doing
sentences.zh: 这给了共和党人在该州卷土重来的机会，如果共和党人能在弗吉尼亚州获胜，这可能预示着他们在

sentences.en: much better in the midterm elections and even the 2024 presidential.

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So the question in this race or a question in this race is, is this a favorable moment for Republicans
sentences.zh: 所以这场竞选中的一个问题是，这对共和党来说是

sentences.en: nationally or is it still the case coming out of Biden's 10-point victory a year ago that this is a favorable moment for Democrats?
sentences.zh: 全国范围内的有利时机，还是说在拜登一年前取得10个百分点的胜利之后，这仍然是对民主党有利的时刻？

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: During Trump, the national environment was very unfavorable for Republicans.
sentences.zh: 在特朗普执政期间，全国环境对共和党非常不利。

sentences.en: As we saw, Democrats took control of the White House and Congress.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所见，民主党控制了白宫和国会。

sentences.en: And now there's a sense that that could be changing.
sentences.zh: 而现在有一种感觉，这种情况可能会发生变化。

sentences.en: Biden's approval ratings are not what they were when he entered office.
sentences.zh: 拜登的支持率已不如他刚上任时那样高了。

sentences.en: He's doing much worse, particularly with independents.
sentences.zh: 他的表现差了很多，特别是在独立选民中。

sentences.en: And Republicans see a real opportunity.
sentences.zh: 共和党人看到了真正的机会。

sentences.en: They're looking at the environment around them and they're seeing that people are facing all these challenges in their daily lives.
sentences.zh: 他们审视周围的环境，看到人们在日常生活中面临着所有这些挑战。

sentences.en: There's been an uptick in crime.
sentences.zh: 犯罪率有所上升。

sentences.en: There's a rise in inflation.
sentences.zh: 通货膨胀加剧。

sentences.en: So people's prices for gas, for cars, for milk, for groceries are higher.
sentences.zh: 所以人们购买汽油、汽车、牛奶和杂货的价格更高了。

sentences.en: There's a supply chain shortage.
sentences.zh: 存在供应链短缺。

sentences.en: There's concerns about how everyone's going to get their Christmas presents, things like that.
sentences.zh: 人们担心如何买到圣诞礼物，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And Republicans see those as issues that they can capitalize on to really make a comeback in the midterMs.
sentences.zh: 共和党人认为这些是他们可以利用的问题，从而在中期选举中真正卷土重来。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So that is the national backdrop for this state governor's race that everyone's watching so closely.
sentences.zh: 这就是每个人都密切关注的这场州长竞选的全国背景。

sentences.en: So tell us about the candidates in that race.
sentences.zh: 那么请告诉我们这场竞选中的候选人情况。

sentences.en: So Terry McAuliffe is the Democratic candidate who's running.
sentences.zh: 特里·麦考利夫是参选的民主党候选人。

sentences.zh: 你知道，当你当选州长时，你不是作为民主党州长或共和党州长当选的。

sentences.en: You're elected governor of the entire state.
sentences.zh: 你是作为整个州的州长当选的。

sentences.en: He's a former governor of Virginia.
sentences.zh: 他是弗吉尼亚州的前州长。

sentences.en: Virginia has this quirky law where you can't run for two consecutive terMs. So he's back for a second term out of being out of office for four years.
sentences.zh: 弗吉尼亚州有一项古怪的法律，规定你不能连续两届竞选。所以他在离任四年后又回来竞选第二个任期。

sentences.en: The second I took that oath to office, I got out of bed trying to help everybody.
sentences.zh: 我宣誓就职的那一刻起，我就起床努力帮助每一个人。

sentences.en: He's a longtime party stalwart.
sentences.zh: 他是长期的党内中坚力量。

sentences.en: He's someone who's close friends with the Clintons.
sentences.zh: 他是与克林顿夫妇关系密切的人。

sentences.en: He was a very, very prominent party fundraiser for many, many years.
sentences.zh: 多年来，他一直是一位非常、非常著名的党内筹款人。

sentences.en: So he's someone that has long relationships in the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 所以他在民主党内有着长期的关系。

sentences.en: Who is it's going to raise teacher pay?

sentences.en: Who is it's going to get broadband access?
sentences.zh: 谁会实现宽带接入？

sentences.en: My politics are about helping people, lifting everybody up.

sentences.en: But we got to get Democrats out to vote.

sentences.en: We are facing a lot of headwinds from Washington.

sentences.en: As you know, the president is unpopular today, unfortunately, here in Virginia.
sentences.zh: 如你所知，总统今天在弗吉尼亚州并不受欢迎，很遗憾。

sentences.en: So we have got to plow through.
sentences.zh: 所以我们必须努力克服。

sentences.en: That his campaign was facing a lot of headwinds from Washington and saying that the president isn't popular.
sentences.zh: 他的竞选团队正面临来自华盛顿的许多阻力，并且他说总统并不受欢迎。

sentences.en: We're tired of the chitty chat up in Washington.
sentences.zh: 我们厌倦了华盛顿的闲言碎语。

sentences.zh: 他也非常、非常直言不讳地表示国会需要通过基础设施法案。

sentences.en: I'm traveling all over Virginia.
sentences.zh: 我走遍了弗吉尼亚州。

sentences.en: They're worried about minimum wage.
sentences.zh: 他们担心最低工资问题。

sentences.en: They want elderly care.
sentences.zh: 他们想要老年护理。

sentences.en: They want to see paid sick leave, family medical leave.
sentences.zh: 他们希望看到带薪病假、家庭医疗假。

sentences.en: And that that is something that would really help his campaign if they could get those things done before his election.
sentences.zh: 如果能在选举前完成这些事情，那对他竞选确实会有很大帮助。

sentences.en: And the frustration is, why isn't it done by now?
sentences.zh: 而令人沮丧的是，为什么到现在还没完成？

sentences.en: 69 votes in the Senate two months ago.

sentences.en: Get it done this week.
sentences.zh: 这周就把它完成。

sentences.en: Do your job.
sentences.zh: 做好你们的工作。

sentences.en: So although McAuliffe seems to be acknowledging there are problems with being a close ally of Joe
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管麦考利夫似乎承认作为乔·拜登的亲密盟友存在问题，

sentences.en: Biden, he's still betting that there's a fair bit of goodwill among Virginia voters for the president and for the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 他仍然押注弗吉尼亚州选民对总统和民主党仍有相当多的善意。

sentences.en: And his message is, you know, give this party, give this president, give me a chance.
sentences.zh: 他的信息是，你知道，给这个党，给这位总统，给我一个机会。

sentences.en: We're on the right track.
sentences.zh: 我们走在正确的轨道上。

sentences.en: Right.

sentences.zh: 有趣的是，他并没有回避拜登。

sentences.zh: 他仍然拥抱“拜登民主党人”的旗号。

sentences.en: He's just kind of saying that he would like to see them get a bit more done in Washington.
sentences.zh: 他只是说他希望看到他们在华盛顿多做一点实事。

sentences.zh: 他真正关注的是试图让唐纳德·特朗普在这次选举中继续作为一个角色存在。

sentences.zh: 让我们从格伦竞选的开始说起。

sentences.zh: 他启动竞选时提出了一个选举诚信计划，该计划基于唐纳德·特朗普关于2020年选举的阴谋论。

sentences.en: Warning that should Republicans win, that they would bring this state back to Trump-like policies, to some form of Trumpism.
sentences.zh: 警告说如果共和党人获胜，他们会将这个州带回特朗普式的政策，带回某种形式的特朗普主义。

sentences.en: You got to ask yourself, why is it that Glenn Youngkin and Donald Trump are so close?
sentences.zh: 你得问问自己，为什么格伦·扬金和唐纳德·特朗普如此亲近？

sentences.en: Because they share the same agenda.
sentences.zh: 因为他们有着相同的议程。

sentences.zh: 你最好相信那个议程与弗吉尼亚人完全脱节。

sentences.en: It's an open question whether that is really going to resonate with voters who just aren't seeing that much Donald Trump in their daily lives.

sentences.zh: 我是格伦·扬金。

sentences.zh: 我不是政客。

sentences.zh: 他是一位前私募股权高管。

sentences.zh: 在北弗吉尼亚生活了26年并拥有长期的商业生涯后，去年夏天我从椅子上站起来说，够了，受够了。

sentences.en: My beloved Commonwealth is just being driven into the ditch by the leadership in Richmond.
sentences.zh: 我深爱的联邦州正被里士满的领导层带入沟里。

sentences.en: He's never held political office before, which means he doesn't have much of a record for McAuliffe to go after.

sentences.en: That makes him a much more difficult target for
sentences.zh: 这使他成为民主党人一个更难对付的目标。

sentences.en: Democrats.

sentences.en: He's also the kind of politician that Virginia voters tend to like, a sort of outsider businessman they believe can come in and shake things up in the state.
sentences.zh: 弗吉尼亚州迎来了新的一天，未来属于我们，而不是他们。

sentences.en: It's a new day here in Virginia, and the future belongs to us, not them.
sentences.zh: 他与唐纳德·特朗普跳了一场非常迷人的舞蹈，他拥抱了特朗普主义的许多旗号。

sentences.en: And 80% is enough for them, because they want to win the state.
sentences.zh: 但是丽莎，这仍然让扬金面临一个看似数学上的难题。

sentences.en: It's also exactly what his campaign needs to do, because they know if they give 100% to these Trump conservatives, they risk
sentences.zh: 如果他想弥补拜登在弗吉尼亚州领先特朗普的10个百分点的差距，他就需要争取到大量的温和派选民。

sentences.en: losing moderates, and that could cost them this election.
sentences.zh: 那么扬金的策略是什么？

sentences.en: But Lisa, that still leaves Youngkin with what seems like a math problem.
sentences.zh: 嗯，扬金的竞选团队和弗吉尼亚州所有参与这次竞选的人都意识到，谁能让更多的选民去投票，谁就会获胜，

sentences.en: He needs to peel off a lot of moderate voters in Virginia if he's going to make up for the 10-point gap that Biden had over Trump in the state.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一场非大选年的选举，投票率会很低。

sentences.en: And so what is Youngkin's strategy to do that?
sentences.zh: 所以最能激励其基本盘的一方很可能会成为赢家。

sentences.en: Well, Youngkin's campaign recognizes, as does everyone involved with this campaign in Virginia,
sentences.zh: 因此，他开始通过转向这个历史上并没有大规模激励选民的问题来激励他的基本盘。

sentences.en: that whoever gets most of their voters to the polls will win, that this is an off-off-year election, and turnout is going to be low.
sentences.zh: 这曾经是一个比较冷门的问题，是候选人会谈论但并没有真正将其作为整个竞选核心的问题，那就是教育和学校。

sentences.en: So the side that can best motivate their base will likely come out of this, the winner.
sentences.zh: 扬金利用了家长们在过去一年的疫情中对孩子上学问题感到愤怒和沮丧的情绪。

sentences.en: And so he's started to motivate his base by turning to this issue that really historically hasn't motivated voters in massive numbers.
sentences.zh: 他利用了这种情绪。

sentences.en: It's been sort of a sleepier issue, something that candidates talked about, but didn't really center their whole campaigns around, and that is education and schools.
sentences.zh: 他利用了这种情绪。

sentences.en: Youngkin has capitalized on the sense that parents have spent the last year of this pandemic stewing in rage and frustration over their kids' schooling.
sentences.zh: 他利用了这种情绪。

sentences.en: There is a revolt against the way our schools have been managed comprehensively.
sentences.zh: 人们对我们学校的管理方式感到非常不满，这是一种全面的反抗。

sentences.en: I would not have a vaccine passport in Virginia.
sentences.zh: 我不会在弗吉尼亚州推行疫苗护照。

sentences.en: I don't believe in it.
sentences.zh: 我不相信那一套。

sentences.en: I think we have to respect parents' decisions about their own children.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们必须尊重家长对自己孩子的决定。

sentences.en: And I'd stop teaching them what to think and teach them how to think.
sentences.zh: 我会停止教他们“想什么”，而是教他们“怎么想”。

sentences.en: So we've watched critical race theory come into our schools and try to divide our children based on seeing everything through a lens as opposed to the content of their character.
sentences.zh: 我们看到批判性种族理论进入了我们的学校，试图通过某种视角来看待一切，而不是关注孩子们的品格，以此来分裂我们的孩子。

sentences.en: And so what Youngkin's campaign sees is an ability to motivate the conservative part of his base
sentences.zh: 杨金的竞选团队认为，他们有能力激励保守派选民基础，

sentences.en: around issues that really are sort of these pet issues of conservatives, things like critical race theory, how transgender students are treated in schools.
sentences.zh: 围绕那些真正属于保守派关切的问题，比如批判性种族理论，以及跨性别学生在学校如何被对待等问题。

sentences.en: And then he's hoping that he can peel off some of these moderate voters, particularly in these really voter-rich suburbs, with issues around mask
sentences.zh: 他希望通过口罩强制令、学校公共卫生准则以及儿童疫苗强制令等问题，

sentences.en: mandates and public health guidelines for schools and vaccine mandates for children.
sentences.zh: 争取到一些温和派选民，特别是在那些选民众多的郊区。

sentences.en: Then something happened that really let Youngkin capitalize on this argument that he's been making around schools and could potentially alter the dynamics of this race.
sentences.zh: 随后发生了一件事，让杨金能够利用他一直在学校问题上提出的论点，并可能改变这场竞选的态势。

sentences.en: In the second debate between the candidates...
sentences.zh: 在候选人之间的第二场辩论中……

sentences.en: Good evening, I'm Chuck Todd, and welcome to the Virginia gubernatorial debate between Democrats...
sentences.zh: 晚上好，我是查克·托德，欢迎收看民主党人之间的弗吉尼亚州州长辩论……

sentences.en: They were discussing issues around schools and education.
sentences.zh: 他们当时正在讨论学校和教育相关的问题。

sentences.en: What we've seen over the course of the last 20 months is our school systems refusing to engage with parents.
sentences.zh: 在过去的20个月里，我们看到我们的学校系统拒绝与家长沟通。

sentences.en: And what had happened was Youngkin attacked McAuliffe over his veto of a bill from 2017...
sentences.zh: 事情的起因是杨金就麦考利夫2017年否决的一项法案对他进行了攻击……

sentences.en: And in fact, you vetoed the bill that would have allowed parents to opt out of letting their children study material that the parents felt was sexually explicit.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你否决了那项法案，该法案本可以让家长选择不让他们的孩子学习家长认为色情露骨的材料。

sentences.en: And the dispute was prompted by a mother who objected to her son, who was a high school senior, reading things
sentences.zh: 这场争议是由一位母亲引发的，她反对她读高三的儿子阅读某些内容，

sentences.en: that were really part of the canon, literary canon, including Toni Morrison's Beloved.
sentences.zh: 而这些内容实际上是文学经典的一部分，包括托妮·莫里森的《宠儿》。

sentences.en: It became as the Beloved bill.
sentences.zh: 这后来被称为“《宠儿》法案”。

sentences.en: McAuliffe vetoed it.
sentences.zh: 麦考利夫否决了它。

sentences.en: You believe school systems should tell children what to do.
sentences.zh: 你认为学校系统应该告诉孩子们该做什么。

sentences.en: I believe parents should be in charge of their kids' education.
sentences.zh: 我认为家长应该负责孩子的教育。

sentences.en: Mr. McAuliffe, 30 seconds.
sentences.zh: 麦考利夫先生，你有30秒时间。

sentences.en: So first of all, this shows how clueless Glenn Youngkin is.
sentences.zh: 首先，这表明格伦·杨金是多么无知。

sentences.en: He doesn't understand what the laws were because he's never been involved here in helping Virginia.
sentences.zh: 他不了解法律是什么，因为他从未参与过帮助弗吉尼亚州的工作。

sentences.en: Defending his veto, he shot back saying that...
sentences.zh: 为了捍卫自己的否决权，他反击说……

sentences.en: I'm not going to let parents come into schools and actually take books out and make their own decision.
sentences.zh: 我不会让家长进入学校随意撤走书籍并做出他们自己的决定。

sentences.en: You vetoed it.
sentences.zh: 你否决了它。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I've stopped the bill that I don't think parents should be telling schools what they should teach.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我阻止了那项法案，我不认为家长应该告诉学校他们应该教什么。

sentences.en: But, you know...
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道……

sentences.en: He did not believe parents should be telling schools what they teach.
sentences.zh: 他不认为家长应该告诉学校他们教什么。

sentences.en: And he's stood by that statement since, but...
sentences.zh: 从那以后他一直坚持这一立场，但是……

sentences.en: We're being joined live by Republican candidate Glenn Youngkin.
sentences.zh: 共和党候选人格伦·杨金正在直播连线。

sentences.en: Immediately after the debate, Youngkin's campaign took this line and started playing it basically on a loop in front of his voters.
sentences.zh: 辩论结束后，杨金的竞选团队立即抓住了这句话，并开始在选民面前循环播放。

sentences.en: Terry McAuliffe last night actually said that parents shouldn't have anything to say about their children's education.
sentences.zh: 特里·麦考利夫昨晚竟然说，家长不应该对孩子的教育有任何发言权。

sentences.en: He believes in government.
sentences.zh: 他相信政府。

sentences.en: He believes in bureaucrats.
sentences.zh: 他相信官僚。

sentences.en: He believes in politicians
sentences.zh: 他相信政客，

sentences.en: should be standing between parents and children.
sentences.zh: 应该站在家长和孩子之间。

sentences.en: My opponent does not respect parents.
sentences.zh: 我的对手不尊重家长。

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 我尊重。

sentences.en: And the reason Youngkin's campaign sees that comment as such a powerful part of their closing
sentences.zh: 杨金的竞选团队之所以认为这条评论是他们结语中如此有力的一部分，

sentences.en: message is because it really encapsulates a lot of what they've been trying to say about
sentences.zh: 是因为它真正概括了他们一直试图传达的关于麦考利夫的很多信息，

sentences.en: Mr. McAuliffe, that he would side with the government over parents and a whole host of issues that could energize the entire coalition of the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 即在许多问题上，他会站在政府一边而不是家长一边，这可以激发整个共和党联盟的活力。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用一个月，且无需绑定信用卡，去探索《时报》呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So, Lisa, you described a moment in the governor's debate that Youngkin seized on and used to frame McAuliffe as someone who believes that government, rather than parents,
sentences.zh: 那么，丽莎，你描述了州长辩论中的一个时刻，杨金抓住了这个机会，把麦考利夫塑造成一个认为政府而不是家长，

sentences.en: should be deciding what happens in schools.
sentences.zh: 应该决定学校里发生什么的人。

sentences.en: What has been the reaction from voters to that line of attack from Youngkin?
sentences.zh: 选民对杨金的这种攻击方式有什么反应？

sentences.en: Well, what we've seen from Republicans, at least, is that it's been pretty powerful, that he is giving Republicans exactly what they want to hear.
sentences.zh: 嗯，至少从共和党人那里我们看到，这非常有效，他给了共和党人他们想听的内容。

sentences.en: I went to see him at a campaign rally last week in Winchester, which is a small town that's in one of these fast-growing exurban counties,
sentences.zh: 上周我在温彻斯特参加了他的竞选集会，那是一个位于快速发展的城郊县之一的小镇，

sentences.en: made my way through the crowd and talked to a bunch of people who were there.
sentences.zh: 我穿过人群，和那里的一群人聊了聊。

sentences.en: And what really stood out is that a lot of people said that schools were their number one issue.
sentences.zh: 真正引人注目的是，很多人说学校是他们最关心的问题。

sentences.en: My top issues, critical race theory in our schools, the vaccine mandates.
sentences.zh: 我最关心的问题是学校里的批判性种族理论和疫苗强制令。

sentences.en: They were worried about what they were seeing in schools.
sentences.zh: 他们担心自己在学校里看到的情况。

sentences.en: The more I've listened and paid attention and I've seen what's going on in Loudoun County and I see what's going on in Frederick County,
sentences.zh: 我听得越多，关注得越多，我看到了劳登县和弗雷德里克县正在发生的事情，

sentences.en: you know, the stuff I see, I don't want corrupting my children.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我看到的东西，我不希望它腐蚀我的孩子。

sentences.en: I want them to be strong in what they believe and what they know.
sentences.zh: 我希望他们在自己的信仰和知识上坚定不移。

sentences.en: I spoke to this one woman who was saying how she didn't want to have to, she was vaccinated, she did not want to be forced to vaccinate her children.
sentences.zh: 我和一位女士交谈，她说她不想被迫接种疫苗，她也不想被迫给孩子接种疫苗。

sentences.en: To see these poor kids, masked up, scared to death of the virus, that has a 99.89 survival rate will hardly affect them at all.
sentences.zh: 看到这些可怜的孩子戴着口罩，被病毒吓得要死，而病毒的存活率高达99.89%，几乎不会影响他们。

sentences.en: And I'm like putting fear in them.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这简直是在给他们制造恐惧。

sentences.en: And are you going to vaccinate or you're on the fence?
sentences.zh: 你是打算接种疫苗，还是还在犹豫？

sentences.en: I'm not planning to vaccinate.
sentences.zh: 我不打算接种疫苗。

sentences.en: You're not.
sentences.zh: 你不打算？

sentences.en: No, no, they're not.
sentences.zh: 不，不，他们不打算。

sentences.en: No, they're not.
sentences.zh: 不，他们不打算。

sentences.en: And the school, I'm sure, doesn't have any, like, mandate.
sentences.zh: 而且学校，我敢肯定，没有任何强制令。

sentences.en: Not, I mean, not right now.
sentences.zh: 不，我是说，目前还没有。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And if Glenn Youngkin gets in, they won't.
sentences.zh: 如果格伦·杨金当选，他们就不会有了。

sentences.en: When he gets in, they won't.
sentences.zh: 当他当选后，就不会有了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: I appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.en: She was worried about the long-term impacts of vaccinating them and was worried that should McAuliffe win, he would impose a vaccine mandate for kids.
sentences.zh: 她担心给孩子接种疫苗的长期影响，并担心如果麦考利夫获胜，他会强制要求孩子接种疫苗。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Is there any evidence to support that?
sentences.zh: 有什么证据支持这一点吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, McAuliffe has said that he supports mask and vaccine mandates for students, teachers, and school staff, like governors in a lot of liberal states do.
sentences.zh: 是的，麦考利夫曾表示，他支持学生、教师和学校员工的口罩和疫苗强制令，就像许多自由派州的州长所做的那样。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Youngkin has said that he encourages Virginians to get vaccinated, but he doesn't support mandates.
sentences.zh: 杨金表示他鼓励弗吉尼亚人接种疫苗，但他不支持强制令。

sentences.en: I think the important context here with things like mask mandates and vaccine mandates is they are really popular with the broader electorate.
sentences.zh: 我认为关于口罩强制令和疫苗强制令，这里重要的背景是它们在广大选民中确实很受欢迎。

sentences.en: There's very few issues where, in American political life right now, where you see support from 60 or 70 percent of the population.
sentences.zh: 在美国目前的政治生活中，很少有议题能得到60%或70%人口的支持。

sentences.en: And that's what you see when you ask questions about whether people should be required to wear masks in schools, or teachers should be required to get vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 当你询问人们是否应该要求在学校佩戴口罩，或者是否应该要求教师接种疫苗时，你看到的就是这种情况。

sentences.en: There is broad support for that.
sentences.zh: 对此有广泛的支持。

sentences.en: But when you look at the numbers within Republican voters, they're much, much lower.
sentences.zh: 但当你观察共和党选民内部的数据时，支持率要低得多。

sentences.en: A third of Republican voters support proposals like that.
sentences.zh: 只有三分之一的共和党选民支持这样的提议。

sentences.en: So what Youngkin is trying to do is split the difference on this issue and cast himself as someone who's supportive of vaccines, but against mandates.
sentences.zh: 所以杨金试图在这个问题上折中，把自己塑造成一个支持疫苗但反对强制令的人。

sentences.en: And it has been a difficult line to walk.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一条很难走的路线。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I'm curious how McAuliffe has been responding to Youngkin's strategy in these past few weeks of focusing on education and parents, critical race theory,
sentences.zh: 我很好奇麦考利夫在过去几周里是如何回应杨金专注于教育、家长、批判性种族理论的策略的，

sentences.en: and this accusation that Democrats are trying to come between parents and their children.
sentences.zh: 以及关于民主党试图介入家长和孩子之间的指控。

sentences.en: Well, he's dismissed all the outrage surrounding critical race theory as racist and divisive and a dog whistle for the Trump base.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他驳斥了所有围绕批判性种族理论的愤怒，称其为种族主义、分裂性的，是针对特朗普选民基础的“狗哨”政治。

sentences.en: But there are signs that his campaign senses some danger in this line of attack.
sentences.zh: 但有迹象表明，他的竞选团队感受到了这种攻击路线带来的危险。

sentences.en: He's returned to highlighting his education proposals.
sentences.zh: 他重新开始强调他的教育提案。

sentences.en: That was the first policy that he put out when he announced his campaign.
sentences.zh: 那是他宣布竞选时提出的第一个政策。

sentences.en: And that's really to undercut any argument that Youngkin could be stronger on the issue.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是为了削弱杨金在这一议题上可能比他更强的任何论点。

sentences.en: And he's talking about things that are included in his plan, like promising to invest $2 billion in education, raise teacher pay, expand pre-K programs in the state.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了他计划中包含的内容，比如承诺投资20亿美元用于教育，提高教师工资，扩大州内的学前班项目。

sentences.en: He also released an ad saying that Youngkin would cut billions of dollars in education funding and bring Donald Trump and Betsy DeVos' education policies back to Virginia.
sentences.zh: 他还发布了一则广告，称杨金会削减数十亿美元的教育经费，并将唐纳德·特朗普和贝齐·德沃斯的教育政策带回弗吉尼亚州。

sentences.en: So he's trying to tie Youngkin to Trump on these issues while being supportive of vaccine mandates and trying to sort of dismiss critical race theory.
sentences.zh: 所以他试图在这些问题上将杨金与特朗普联系起来，同时支持疫苗强制令，并试图淡化批判性种族理论。

sentences.en: Lisa, you had said that this subject, education, and that debate moment,
sentences.zh: 丽莎，你曾说教育这个主题，以及那个辩论时刻，

sentences.en: could alter the dynamics of this race.
sentences.zh: 可能会改变这场竞选的态势。

sentences.en: So how much has all of this actually influenced the race so far?
sentences.zh: 那么到目前为止，这一切对竞选的影响有多大？

sentences.en: What do the polls tell us?
sentences.zh: 民调告诉我们什么？

sentences.en: Well, look, this is a hard race to poll because nobody knows exactly what turnout is going to be.
sentences.zh: 嗯，看，这是一场很难进行民调的竞选，因为没人知道最终投票率会是多少。

sentences.en: It's the first competitive election, as we said, of the Biden administration.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，这是拜登政府执政以来的第一次竞争性选举。

sentences.en: But we do know that earlier in September,
sentences.zh: 但我们确实知道，在9月初，

sentences.en: McAuliffe seemed like he was up by a greater amount, maybe nine points or seven points, five points.
sentences.zh: 麦考利夫看起来领先优势更大，可能是九个百分点，或者七个、五个百分点。

sentences.en: And since that debate moment, the race has tightened.
sentences.zh: 而自那次辩论之后，选情变得胶着了。

sentences.en: And there was one poll in particular that came shortly after the debate that showed the candidates effectively tied that just set off alarm bills
sentences.zh: 特别是在辩论后不久出现的一项民调显示，两位候选人实际上打成了平手，这拉响了警报，

sentences.en: and really some panic in Democratic circles.
sentences.zh: 并在民主党圈子里引起了一些恐慌。

sentences.en: And since then, what we've seen is this flotilla of Democratic heavy hitters heading into the state.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，我们看到一大批民主党重量级人物涌入该州。

sentences.en: Former President Barack Obama is going to be coming in.
sentences.zh: 前总统巴拉克·奥巴马即将到来。

sentences.en: So will Stacey Abrams, who, of course, ran for governor in Georgia.
sentences.zh: 斯泰西·艾布拉姆斯也会来，她当然曾在佐治亚州竞选过州长。

sentences.en: Jill Biden's going to be coming in for McAuliffe.
sentences.zh: 吉尔·拜登将为麦考利夫助阵。

sentences.en: Speaker Nancy Pelosi hosted a fundraiser for him.
sentences.zh: 众议院议长南希·佩洛西为他举办了一场筹款活动。

sentences.en: So those are all signs of real alarm among Democrats about where this race is going.
sentences.zh: 所以这些都是民主党人对这场竞选走向感到真正恐慌的迹象。

sentences.en: Alarm that McAuliffe could lose to Yunkin.
sentences.zh: 担心麦考利夫可能会输给杨金。

sentences.en: And for all the reasons you said earlier, that would be a very problematic symbol for the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 基于你之前所说的所有原因，那将是民主党的一个非常麻烦的象征。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I think what people in the White House are concerned about is that it could undercut support for Biden's agenda in Congress.
sentences.zh: 我认为白宫的人担心的是，这可能会削弱国会对拜登议程的支持。

sentences.en: Biden is still negotiating these really complicated pieces of legislation that make up his entire domestic agenda, pretty much.
sentences.zh: 拜登仍在就这些非常复杂的立法进行谈判，这些立法几乎构成了他整个国内议程的全部。

sentences.en: And if he loses in Virginia, you could start to see an impact where these Democrats who are, you know, in the House or in the Senate who are up for reelection might say, well,
sentences.zh: 如果他在弗吉尼亚州落败，你可能会开始看到一种影响，即那些在众议院或参议院面临连任的民主党人可能会说，好吧，

sentences.en: what Virginia tells me is that running on this Biden agenda isn't all that good for me.
sentences.zh: 弗吉尼亚州的情况告诉我，推行拜登的议程对我来说并不是什么好事。

sentences.en: So it could undercut Biden's political capital, as well as sending shockwaves of alarm among all these candidates who are going to face what are already expected to be competitive
sentences.zh: 因此，这可能会削弱拜登的政治资本，并在所有明年预计将面临竞争性选举的候选人中引发恐慌。

sentences.en: elections next year.
sentences.zh: 选举明年就要到了。

sentences.en: And what would it mean for Republicans if this race remains very close and if Yunkin were to defeat McAuliffe, which would be a meaningful upset?
sentences.zh: 如果这场竞选保持非常胶着，如果杨金击败了麦考利夫，这将是一场重大的冷门，这对共和党人意味着什么？

sentences.en: It would be a very, very meaningful upset.
sentences.zh: 这将是一场非常、非常有意义的冷门。

sentences.en: It would be the first time Republicans win in
sentences.zh: 这将是共和党人十二年来首次在

sentences.en: Virginia in a dozen years.
sentences.zh: 弗吉尼亚州获胜。

sentences.en: It would be a major feather in their cap.
sentences.zh: 这将是他们的一大功绩。

sentences.en: It would probably lead to a huge influx of money because you'd see this surge of enthusiasm among Republican donors who would
sentences.zh: 这可能会导致大量资金涌入，因为你会看到共和党捐赠者中出现这种热情高涨的局面，他们会

sentences.en: see that control of Congress could be in their grasp in next year's midterMs. And it would also,
sentences.zh: 看到明年中期选举中控制国会可能就在他们的掌握之中。而且，

sentences.en: I think, cause a lot of these candidates who are running in the midterms to try to steal the
sentences.zh: 我认为，这也会导致许多参加中期选举的候选人试图窃取

sentences.en: Yunkin playbook to run on schools.
sentences.zh: 杨金的剧本，以学校问题作为竞选议题。

sentences.en: I suspect we'll already be hearing about schools in the midterMs. If Yunkin wins, I think it'll be an inescapable part of every Republican's message.
sentences.zh: 我怀疑我们已经会在中期选举中听到关于学校的问题了。如果杨金获胜，我认为这将成为每个共和党人信息中不可避免的一部分。

sentences.en: Lisa, I wonder if there's a sense that Democrats could, in theory, re-alter the dynamics of this race
sentences.zh: 丽莎，我想知道是否有一种感觉，即民主党在理论上可以通过改变弗吉尼亚等地选民目前看待民主党的方式，

sentences.en: by changing the way voters in places like Virginia see the Democratic Party right now, which is by getting big things actually done in Congress before this election.
sentences.zh: 即在选举前在国会真正完成大事，来重新改变这场竞选的态势。

sentences.en: It's in theory possible that the president's infrastructure bill and his sweeping expansion of the social safety net could all get passed before early November.
sentences.zh: 理论上，总统的基础设施法案和他对社会安全网的全面扩张有可能在11月初之前全部通过。

sentences.en: And wouldn't that mean that McAuliffe and Biden and
sentences.zh: 那难道不意味着麦考利夫、拜登和

sentences.en: Democrats could go to voters and say, we have something real that we have done for you.
sentences.zh: 民主党人可以告诉选民，我们已经为你做了一些实实在在的事情。

sentences.en: And that's bigger than your fears of what's happening in schools.
sentences.zh: 而这比你对学校里发生的事情的恐惧更重要。

sentences.en: Is this something that Democrats think might seal the deal for McAuliffe and make this race a template for Democratic success in the midterms and over the next few years?
sentences.zh: 这是民主党人认为可能为麦考利夫锁定胜局，并使这场竞选成为民主党在中期选举及未来几年取得成功的模板吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: If Democrats can get something passed in Congress or even make progress towards a deal to get something passed in Congress over the next two weeks, that would help McAuliffe.
sentences.zh: 如果民主党能在未来两周内让国会通过某项法案，或者至少在达成协议以通过法案方面取得进展，那将对麦考利夫有所帮助。

sentences.en: That would be great for McAuliffe.
sentences.zh: 这对麦考利夫来说会很棒。

sentences.en: And it would give them something to run on.
sentences.zh: 这也能让他们有竞选的筹码。

sentences.en: At this point, that doesn't look super likely, but the school issue is not going away.
sentences.zh: 目前看来，这不太可能实现，但学校问题不会就此消失。

sentences.en: For American parents, this is their third year of schooling during a pandemic.
sentences.zh: 对于美国父母来说，这是他们在疫情期间经历的第三个学年。

sentences.en: It is something that is ingrained at this point in every American household with kids.
sentences.zh: 这一点已经深入到每个有孩子的美国普通家庭中。

sentences.en: And you have this situation where you have Republicans, they've seized on this issue that is really resonant and visceral in a lot of American households.
sentences.zh: 现在的情况是，共和党人抓住了这个在许多美国家庭中极具共鸣和切身感的问题。

sentences.en: And they're defining the terms of it.
sentences.zh: 并且他们正在定义这个问题的内涵。

sentences.en: A few months ago, it was about keeping schools open.
sentences.zh: 几个月前，重点还是关于保持学校开放。

sentences.en: Then they've talked more or less about critical race theory.
sentences.zh: 后来他们或多或少地谈论了批判性种族理论。

sentences.en: Now the focus is really on masks and vaccine mandates in schools.
sentences.zh: 现在焦点真正转向了学校的口罩和疫苗强制令。

sentences.en: But if this issue that Republicans are defining helps them win Virginia, change the national political environment,
sentences.zh: 但如果共和党所定义的这个问题能帮助他们赢得弗吉尼亚州，改变全国政治环境，

sentences.en: and gives them the edge heading into the midterms next year, it could just be the thing that potentially helps Republicans win back control of Congress.
sentences.zh: 并让他们在明年的中期选举中占据优势，这可能正是帮助共和党夺回国会控制权的关键因素。

sentences.en: Lisa, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 丽莎，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: Over the weekend, a gang in Haiti known for mass kidnappings abducted a group of 17 American and
sentences.zh: 周末，海地一个以大规模绑架而闻名的帮派劫持了一群17名美国和

sentences.en: Canadian missionaries, as well as members of their families, in the latest sign of lawlessness in the country.
sentences.zh: 加拿大传教士，以及他们的家人，这是该国无法无天的最新迹象。

sentences.en: The abduction occurred as the missionaries, Christians who mostly traveled to
sentences.zh: 绑架事件发生时，这些传教士——大多是从俄亥俄州前往

sentences.en: Haiti from Ohio, were returning from a trip to an orphanage.
sentences.zh: 海地的基督徒——正结束对一家孤儿院的访问返回途中。

sentences.en: Kidnappings and violence have exploded in Haiti in the months since the assassination of the country's president.
sentences.zh: 自海地总统遇刺后的几个月里，绑架和暴力事件在海地激增。

sentences.en: And British authorities say they are treating the murder of a member of parliament as an act of terrorism.
sentences.zh: 英国当局表示，他们将一名议员的遇害视为恐怖主义行为。

sentences.en: The lawmaker,
sentences.zh: 这位议员，

sentences.en: David Amos, was meeting on Friday with constituents in a church building when he was stabbed to death by a
sentences.zh: 大卫·阿梅斯，周五在教堂建筑内会见选民时，被一名

sentences.en: 25-year-old man.
sentences.zh: 25岁的男子刺死。

sentences.en: Police have not named the man who has been arrested, but said they believe his motivation may be linked to Islamic extremism.
sentences.zh: 警方尚未公布被捕男子的姓名，但表示他们认为其动机可能与伊斯兰极端主义有关。

sentences.zh: 今天的节目由罗伯特·杰米森制作，

sentences.zh: 杰西卡·钟、西德尼·哈珀和罗伯·齐普科参与制作。

sentences.zh: 由迈克尔·贝努瓦和丽莎·周编辑，克里斯·伍德负责工程，并包含玛丽安·洛萨诺的原创音乐。

sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由吉姆·

sentences.zh: 这就是今天的《每日新闻》。

sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine, until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作，直到今年夏天，选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场激烈、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《地铁》节目中，我和莎拉·凯尼格将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。
